function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Here’s a quick snapshot of the **next big festivals happening in the United States** (as of June 2026).  All dates are for the 2026 calendar year and are subject to change, so be sure to double‑check the official websites before you book anything.

| # | Festival | Dates (2026) | Location | Genre / Focus | Quick Facts |
|---|----------|--------------|----------|---------------|-------------|
| 1 | **Summerfest** | **July 1–10, 2026** | Milwaukee, WI | Multi‑genre music & cultural celebration | 8‑day event, 70+ stages, ~400,000 attendees |
| 2 | **Lollapalooza Chicago** | **August 4–7, 2026** | Chicago, IL | Alternative/rock, indie, hip‑hop | 4‑day festival, 30+ stages, ~200,000 attendees |
| 3 | **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival** | **May 27–June 5, 2026** | New Orleans, LA | Jazz, blues, world music | 10‑day festival, 200+ stages, ~300,000 attendees |
| 4 | **Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival** | **April 14–16, 2026** | Indio, CA | Indie, rock, hip‑hop, electronic | 3‑day festival, 100+ stages, ~200,000 attendees |
| 5 | **South by Southwest (SXSW)** | **March 11–20, 2026** | Austin, TX | Film, music, interactive media | 10‑day festival, 200+ stages, ~300,000 attendees |
| 6 | **Burning Man** | **August 28–September 5, 2026** | Black Rock Desert, NV | Art, music, community | 9‑day event, ~70,000 participants |
| 7 | **Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival** | **June 23–26, 2026** | Manchester, TN | Rock, indie, hip‑hop, electronic | 4‑day festival, 50+ stages, ~140,000 attendees |

### Why Summerfest is the “next” big thing
- **Timing**: It starts on July 1, just a few weeks after today (June 4, 2026).
- **Scale**: It’s the world’s largest music festival by attendance and number of performances.
- **Accessibility**: Milwaukee is a major city with plenty of accommodation options and public transport.

### Quick links
| Festival | Official Site |
|----------|---------------|
| Summerfest | https://www.summerfest.com |
| Lollapalooza | https://www.lollapalooza.com |
| New Orleans Jazz & Heritage | https://www.nojazzfest.com |
| Coachella | https://www.coachella.com |
| SXSW | https://www.sxsw.com |
| Burning Man | https://burningman.org |
| Bonnaroo | https://bonnaroo.com |

---

#### How to plan
1. **Book early** – Tickets for these festivals sell out fast, especially for the first days.
2. **Check weather** – The Midwest can be hot in July; bring sunscreen and hydration.
3. **Accommodation** – Look for hotels or Airbnb near the venue; consider “festival camping” options if you’re staying on site.
4. **Transportation** – Public transit is often the easiest way to get to and from the festival grounds.
